A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Outlier Gradient Analysis paper, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–D. No material gaps prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5.pdf reports original synthetic-data, vision, NLP, and LLM experiments in Sections 4–7, plus sensitivity, runtime, and distribution-shift results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v7.pdf retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the iForest, L1, and L2 outlier-gradient procedures are unchanged. Both versions also contain the same class-specific LLM estimators and OneClassSVM adaptation for distribution shift.

E1.justification: Both use the same synthetic datasets, CIFAR-10N/100N noise settings, ImageNet subset, four GLUE tasks, three LLM influence benchmarks, and ACS-Income distribution-shift scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including the label-correction and influence baselines, the alternate noisy-learning methods in Table 11, and GEX/TRAK in Table 12.

E3.justification: Sections 4–7 and Appendices B–C retain the same splits, noise rates, sample counts, trimming budgets, model configurations, training schedules, and evaluation metrics. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The trimming-budget and tree-count sensitivity analyses, runtime comparisons, ResNet-18 experiments, distribution-shift tests, and illustrated sample cases are retained with the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both retain five-run vision evaluations and standard deviations in Tables 4 and 9, three-run NLP evaluation in Section 6, and the same uncertainty displays. No run-count, seed, or statistical-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains 96.0% iForest outlier-detection and post-trimming classification accuracy, and Table 3 retains 1.000 ± 0.000 for the proposed method's AUC and recall on all three tasks.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2), Observation 3.1, Hypothesis 3.2, and the computational-complexity expressions in Table 7 are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about connecting detrimental-sample identification to gradient outlier detection, avoiding Hessian computation, and achieving effective and efficient empirical performance.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged. Although the impact heading is renamed, its limitations concerning high-quality data without outliers, trimming-budget selection, algorithm choices, and broader LLM benchmarking remain intact.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same implementation, hyperparameter, and sparse-projection details. Appendix D retains the same code-repository link and hardware, operating-system, and CUDA information; no technical disclosure is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the references retain the same cited works and research positioning. The relationship to influence estimation, self-influence, and other data-centric approaches is unchanged.

P1.justification: On page 9, the numbered heading '10. Broader Impact and Limitations' becomes the unnumbered 'Impact Statement,' with its body unchanged. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the remaining prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4, Tables 1–13, and Algorithm 1 retain their displays, captions, organization, and placement. The figure images are identical, and the heading rename does not reorganize the page layout.

improvement.justification: v7.pdf preserves the scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations of v5.pdf, including its appendices. Renaming the impact heading and updating the version stamp do not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper's overall quality.
